Start the factory

the first session for the two of you, and Scott's own jobs

The first session, for the two of you, and Scott's own jobs beside First jobs. On 16 Nov, 23:04 nothing in the base made power, no miner stood on Iron A, and the boxes held crushed ore and no parts. These jobs go from there, in the order that gets parts soonest. The same on a page of its own: First session.

By the end of the evening

  • Power: 120 MW from the burner station, fed from one box, and a line to every machine of both yards.
  • From the boxes: about 2,954 Iron Ingots and 660 Tin Ingots, and the plates, rods, screws and Concrete you made of them.
  • Hall 1: 45 Iron Ingot, 30 Tin Ingot and 15 Concrete a minute, at half speed.
  • The Foundation yard: its floor, and 30 Iron Ingot and 12.5 Crushed Gangue a minute into two boxes.
  • Not yet: the copper patch on belts, Wind Turbines, the Parts hall. Each row above leaves something running, so stop after any of them.

Known and not known

  • The Stove cooks in this build but stops after the server restarts; that is mended in a build that waits for the last install. Do not plan the evening's food round it.
  • A Biomass Burner Mk.2 is not in this pack. The game's own list has one Biomass Burner, the HUB's two, and nothing else that burns biomass before Tier 3.
  • What the HUB's own two burners give is not in the data. The station's four are counted without them.
  • A belt's price by the metre is not known here. The base game charges it once for every 2 m; if the pack keeps that, Hall 1's belts, the ore belt and the Concrete belt come to about 430 Iron Plate and 430 Screws.
  • Seen in the server's own documents, not in the game what stands, what has no Power Line and what the boxes hold, on 16 Nov, 23:04. If any of it has changed since, the map shows it live.

First jobs: the Foundation yard

for whoever is new: a small yard of your own, in four short jobs

For whoever is new to the game. A small yard of your own on the spare Siterite node east of the lake, built in three short jobs that each leave something running, and a fourth that lays the next hall's floor with what it made. It makes the three things a Foundation costs: Concrete, Iron Plates and Iron Sheets. Every hall still to come stands on Foundations, and no hall of the plan makes Iron Sheets before Tiers 3 and 4. The same jobs, with the game explained from the start, are on a page of their own: First jobs.

The lighter squares are the floor. The number in a corner is the job a piece comes with. Orange lines are belts, with an arrow where the parts arrive; purple dots are Power Poles A, B and C, and the dashed lines their Power Lines. The grid is the world's 8 m grid; the corners carry game coordinates.

  • Where: the node is at -1525, -458, about 90 m east of the ground kept for the Parts hall and 13 m above the camp, on a sand terrace between the lake and a rock ridge.
  • On a floor: 28 Foundations on the world's grid, 6 by 4 from -1568, -448 and 4 more along the south edge from -1552, -416. Its shape is the sand's: rock lies along its west edge and south of its south-west corner. The miner stands on the ground just north of it; everything else stands on it, and its west half is free for a second line.
  • One idea at a time: job 1 is the floor, a miner, a belt, a Crusher, a Smelter, two boxes and power. Job 2 sets a Constructor into each of its two long belts. Job 3 adds a Conveyor Splitter. Nothing built in one job is moved in the next.
  • No settings: every machine stays at 100%. The miner offers 60 ore a minute and the line takes 30, so the Crusher waits half the time. A full box stops the line behind it; nothing breaks.
  • What it takes: on the World map, the Plan panel's What it takes box lists the parts for Foundation yard and for each job, beside what the base's boxes hold. Belts and Power Lines are paid for by length as you lay them and are not in that list.
  • Not known yet: nobody has walked the terrace, so how level it is and whether rock comes up through the floor has to be seen; and which outlet of a Crusher gives which product is read from one Crusher of Scott's, not from the game's data. The belt cards on the map say what to do if it is the other way round.

After the four jobs

  • Keep the three boxes moving. The Lake Bank terrace, the next floor of the build order, is 100 Foundations: 200 Concrete, 100 Iron Sheet, 200 Iron Plate. Each deck of the Lake Works is 285.
  • Twice as much. The miner's east outlet is free, the Crusher works half the time, and the floor's west half is empty but for the burner. A second Smelter and a second Iron Plate Constructor would double the iron and the Concrete. Switch on Edit the plan on the World map and lay it out yourself: the editor knows every machine's size and ports.
  • A Wind Turbine in place of the burner. It needs no fuel and gives 20 to 60 MW depending on how high it stands, which nobody has measured here. It costs 5 Rotor, 15 Iron Rod, 20 Tin Plate, 50 Screws, so it waits for Rotors.
  • A house of your own. The east house of the Twin Houses, on the Grass Fields, is yours: its track is further down this guide.

The Twin Houses

two houses of two storeys, a plaza and a pier on the Grass Fields

A matched pair of two-storey houses with a yard between them on the Grass Fields plateau, 870 m east-north-east of the HUB and about 165 m above it, a bridge from one upper floor to the other, roof terraces, a walk down to the west lake and a pier with a lookout. They are not part of the build order: do them whenever you like. Scott has the west house, in orange FICSIT walls with a Wind Turbine on its roof; his friend has the east one, its mirror image in pine with a harbour lamp. Each track has a home standing once the floor, the ground storey's walls and the furniture are in; everything after that is for when you feel like it.

  • Where: the plot is 88 by 40 m from -968, -608. The yard is 3 by 5 Foundations from -936, -608, the west house 4 by 4 from -968, -608, the east house 4 by 4 from -912, -608. The Lake Walk runs 128 m south from the gate to the west lake; from the pier head a shore walk leads on to the Lakeside power station's causeway.
  • Made of what you have: 283 pieces, every one of them unlocked in your world on 16 Nov 2026 (read from the server's own list) except the kitchens, which wait for Milestone, tier 2: Pioneer Kitchen. The bedrooms and kitchens are our own Quarters and Pioneer Kitchen pieces, upstairs in each house. The map draws each wall, window, door, railing, floor above and lamp at the game's own size, with its level; pick a level in the Plan panel to see one storey at a time. A wall's middle line lies on the Foundation's edge, where the game put your own Metal Walls.
  • The ground: grass at about 160 m, rising and falling by about 3 m across the plot, with a few small rocks; plants on the lake shore stand at 155 to 165 m and a Power Slug on the islet in the lake at 152 m, so the water lies somewhere between 5 and 10 m below the yard. Checked on the map's picture and against the heights of the berries and the crash site round it. Nobody has walked it yet: the first Foundation settles the true height, and how far below the pier the water lies has to be seen.
  • Not tried in the game: that a Foundation snapped onto a 4 m wall puts the next floor 5 m up, which way round the game lays a Ramp on its outline, and SatMap's outlines above the ground. Where the game snaps a piece differently, follow the game: the map shows what goes where, the build gun sets it down.
  • Room to grow: 24 m of grass is kept clear on the outer side of each house, and flat ground 72 m further east, 96 by 64 m from -808, -592, is kept for a second factory; the east road ends on it. Three pure Coal nodes are on the plateau's west edge at -1076, -524; -1136, -504; -1132, -441.
  • Change it: on the World map, switch on Edit the plan: every piece can be moved, turned, taken out or copied, and anything else from the game's list added. The base is a starting point, not a rule.

The Lakeside power station

coal and water power in the lake, 2,000 MW, Tier 4

Coal and water power on a deck in the south-west bay of the west lake, south of the Twin Houses: ten Coal-Powered Generators, 2,000 MW, from one Coal node. The shape is the Rocky Desert Works' coal plant, two rows facing one aisle; the sums are Satisfactory Plus's own. It is a Tier 4 build and no part of the build order above; the plan is here so the water is kept for it.

  • Crush the coal first: here a generator makes 200 MW from 30 m³ of Water a minute and either 20 Coal or 8 Carbon Powder, and a Crusher turns 60 Coal into 40 Carbon Powder. Crushed, the same coal gives two thirds more power: one pure node, 120 Coal a minute, runs ten generators where it would run six.
  • One miner, two outlets, two columns: the Modular Miner gives 60 Coal from each of its two outlets. Each outlet has its own belt, its own Crusher and its own column of five generators, which burn the Crusher's 40 Carbon Powder exactly. No Merger, no balancing, and nothing faster than a Conveyor Belt Mk.1.
  • Two halves that do not depend on each other: each column also has its own Water Extractor, 180 m³ for the 150 its five drink. The west column runs when the east one is not built, or is being changed.
  • Where: the deck is 8 by 7 Foundations from -1072, -352 (56 pieces), with the crusher gallery against its north edge. A causeway two Foundations wide runs north from the gallery to a shore walk along the lake, which joins the bank by the Coal node to the Twin Houses' pier head. The two Water Extractors stand in the lake beside the causeway.
  • On the map: every belt and pipe runs into the machine's real inlet, with each Conveyor Splitter and Pipeline Junction drawn where it stands and saying what passes. Each belt is one straight line from the shore walk to its last generator. The pipes ride 5 m up and pass between the two Crushers.
  • Starting it: the supply is exact, and a generator here stops dead when its fuel runs short. So let each Coal store fill before its column is switched on, and start the extractors (15 MW each) from the power you have. After that the station keeps itself: it uses 41 MW of its own 2,000.
  • Room to grow: the other two pure Coal nodes, at -1076, -523 and -1136, -504, are free: each would run another ten.
  • Not known yet: how deep the water is under the deck and the extractors, how far the lake lies below the plateau (the islet's Power Slug stands at 152 m and the Twin Houses' yard at about 160; an extractor lifts water 10 m), whether Coal needs more than the Standard Mining Head, and whether a Crusher gives a single product by either outlet (the east Crusher's card says what to do if not). The deck's and the gallery's corners are about 4 to 5 m from the islet, the south shore and a small rock. Nobody has walked it.

What is different

nine things that are not like the base game
  • The ores are minerals with new names. Siterite holds iron and tin, Callanite copper and magnesium, Larrussite zinc and silica. Later come Aurovite (caterium), Montanion (cobalt and aluminium) and Kyalite (quartz and salt). In the game data they are the base game's iron, copper, limestone, caterium, bauxite and quartz nodes under new names, so the map you know still applies.
  • Ore is crushed before it is smelted, by hand at first, then in the Crusher. From Tier 1 the Sorter splits the crushed ore further: 24 Crushed Siterite become 18 Crushed Iron, 12 Crushed Tin and 8 Crushed Gangue.
  • Concrete is made from Crushed Gangue, the stone that crushing and sorting leave behind. Three make one Concrete.
  • Tin and bronze come before steel. Tin Plates arrive at HUB Upgrade 4, bronze in Tier 2; steel waits for Tier 3, Basic Steel Production.
  • The miner is modular. A Modular Miner needs a Mining Head: the Standard head gives 30 a minute from each of two outputs, the Hardened head 60, the Diamond head 120. An impure node halves that, a pure node doubles it.
  • No Splitters or Mergers until Tier 1's Logistics Mk. 2. The first lines are straight: one belt, one machine after another.
  • The first power you build is the Biomass Burner (30 MW) or the Wind Turbine Mk1, both at HUB Upgrade 6. The turbine gives 20 to 60 MW depending on how high it stands, and less when other turbines are close.
  • The Space Elevator has a price of its own: 25 Bronze Frame, 75 Modular Frame, 200 Tin Plate, 500 Concrete and 500 Screws. Its first delivery is 75 Smart Plating and 25 Modular Frame.
  • The early game is hand-crafted more than the base game. Tin Plates and Reinforced Iron Plates have no machine until the Assembler in Tier 1.

Every belt between the floors

One row for each run, in the direction it flows. Both ends are exact: a belt of a hall plan where it crosses the hall's edge, a miner on its node, a Splitter or Merger on the rack, or the end of a Storage Container. Click the belt on the plan for its bends, its tier, the first machine it reaches and every crossing. Main Street's rack has 5 lines, 2 m apart and three tiers high; no tier of any line carries two belts over the same stretch.

StageEverything runningTurbines needed, best to worst
Opening28 MW1 to 2

Wind Turbines Mk1 on the plateau south of the camp, about 35 m above it. Each gives 20 to 60 MW depending on how high it stands, and less for every other turbine near it; how near counts is not in the game data. Ten pads are drawn, 28 m apart: build them one at a time and watch what each adds. Until HUB Upgrade 6 unlocks them, see the note under Power below.

Tiers 3 and 4 double the load. 7 turbines carry it at their best; if they give only their minimum, 6 Biomass Burners make up the difference until Tier 4's Advanced Power Infrastructure brings the Wind Turbine Mk2, 60 to 200 MW on the same pads: 2 to 7 of those carry everything.

Tiers 3 and 4: the Lake Works

Tiers 3 and 4: the two-deck works in the lake

The first delivery opens Tiers 3 and 4 together: caterium, molten metal, brass, steel and the Manufacturer. The second delivery asks for 500 Smart Plating, 500 Versatile Framework and 250 Automated Wiring. The Platform works already makes the Smart Plating at 2.25 a minute, so that sets the clock: 222 minutes. Everything here is sized to be ready when the Smart Plating is, the delivery and every part the two tiers cost.

It is one works, and it stands in the lake. The lake is the largest level place beside the camp: 152 by 120 m of open water 16 m north of Hall 1. Two decks of Foundations, one above the other, each 19 by 15: the Foundry on top under the open sky, the Dock works below it. Ore goes up, metal comes down, parts go out. The water the Reformers need is under the floor, and the Air Collector, which collects more the higher it stands, is on the highest floor of the site. Two causeways join it to the camp and to the north shore, so the works is also the bridge across the lake.

How it flows

  1. UpOre crosses the south causeway and rises. Three belts come from the camp over the south causeway, up a Conveyor Lift at the south wall and west along the gallery's south side to the Foundry's west end: 62.2 Siterite Ore a minute from Iron B, 36.7 Callanite Ore from the copper miner's second output and 14.2 Larrussite Ore from the west node. Coal comes from the bunker on the gallery, 10.9 a minute; water up the west wall from the lake, 9.35 m³; air from the collector, 7.03 m³.
  2. Upper deckThe Foundry crushes, sorts, melts and casts. 24 machines, 69.7 MW. Four Flexible Blast Furnaces turn crushed iron, copper and zinc into molten iron, steel and brass; three Reformers cast them into Steel Rods, Steel Ingots and Brass Ingots; Smelters make the iron, tin, copper and zinc ingots the yards cannot cover.
  3. DownMetal goes down through the gallery floor. 9 belts drop 16 m to the Dock's rack at the south wall, each from its own belt of the Foundry: 5.97 Brass Ingot, 27 Copper Ingot, 31.1 Tin Ingot, 5 Concrete, 17.5 Iron Ingot, 21.1 Steel Ingot, 3.56 Zinc Ingot, 14.2 Steel Rod and 8.33 Sand.
  4. Lower deckThe Dock works presses, assembles and manufactures. 31 machines, 64.9 MW. 15 products: the Versatile Framework and Automated Wiring for the delivery, and 13 kinds of parts for the kit below.
  5. OutParts leave through the south wall. At the wall's west end, over 16 m of shallows to the Kit row: 16 Storage Containers side by side on the lake bank north of Main Street, one for each part and one for the spare Concrete. Main Street's rack has no room for 15 more belts and the depot none for the containers. The two delivery parts go on to the Elevator pad by hand.
  6. NorthCaterium comes over the north causeway. The Caterium bench stands on the north shore: 7 machines, 2.4 MW, fed by a belt from the Aurovite node on the hill. It makes 10 Quickwire and 1 Caterium Heatsink a minute, which the furnaces, the Reformers and three milestones cost.

The loops

Nothing in the Foundry is thrown away that something else can use. Every number is what the solver found from the recipes.

LoopWhyWhat goes roundWhat is left

StoneEvery Crusher and Sorter gives Crushed Gangue. The Cast Steel Ingot recipe takes it as flux, and three make one Concrete.Made 88.5 a minute: 8.78 into the steel, 79.7 into Concrete.None. 26.6 Concrete a minute, 5 of it down to the Dock deck for Encased Industrial Beams, the rest to the Kit row.
SlagCasting steel leaves Cold Slag. A Crusher turns slag into Sand, and Steel Pipes are cast in Sand.Slag made 16.3 a minute; 3.69 of it crushed into 7.38 Sand. With the 3.8 Sand the zinc Sorter gives, that covers the Dock's 8.33.12.7 Cold Slag and 2.84 Sand to their containers, then the Sink.

OverflowA machine stops when one of its outputs has nowhere to go. Cold Slag, Crushed Magnesium and spare Sand have no user here.Each passes through a Storage Container on the gallery and on to one AWESOME Sink: the container stays full as stock, the surplus is sunk.The Foundry cannot stall on a by-product. Flue Gas, 14.3 m³ a minute, goes to its stack.

Not known until you try

  • Whether Satisfactory Plus lets Foundations stand over open water exactly as the base game does. If it does not, tell me and the works move to the West Field.
  • How deep the lake is. The Mini Water Extractor needs water under it; the map shows open water where it stands, not the depth.
  • The height of the walls you need. The tallest machine on the lower deck is the Manufacturer, 11 m in the data, so a 16 m storey clears it; the Reformer above is 12 m and the Air Collector 28 m, both under open sky.
  • One square of the lake under the decks, at -1776, -448, shows a shoal on the map. If rock comes up through the lower deck there, a Constructor can move.
  • Which side the ports are on, and where the pipe ports are on a Flexible Blast Furnace and a Reformer. The plans put inlets on one long side and outlets on the other.
  • Whether a full AWESOME Sink line behaves as described. It does in the base game.
  • The shallows between the Dock's south wall and the bank, west of x = -1860: the belts to the Kit row and the spare ingots cross about 16 m of them. If poles will not stand there, lay Foundations.

nine plans, each with a set-up list

Hall plan 1 · Opening

Opening yard, Siterite on Hall 1

2 Crusher, 2 Constructor and 2 Smelter · 15.3 MW · north-west corner -1760, -360

Your first automatic lines. A Modular Miner has two outputs, and until Splitters arrive each output gets a line of its own: a Crusher, a Smelter, and a Constructor that turns the crushed stone into Concrete.

Hall plan 3 · Tier 1

Siterite yard on Hall 1

7 Smelter, 2 Crusher, 2 Constructor and 1 Sorter · 61.6 MW · north-west corner -1760, -360

Iron A is a pure node, so it gives 120 ore a minute where a normal node gives 60. This is the Siterite yard at twice the size: two Crushers, one Sorter at full speed, seven Smelters and two Concrete Constructors, all on Hall 1. Its two ingot belts each pass through a store at the hall's north-west corner before they leave: the Iron store sets the yard's pace, and the Tin store takes the tin that comes with the iron, so the Sorter never stops for it.

A bus hall. Every belt comes in or goes out through the south edge. A rack three belts high runs from that edge down the west wall; each row of machines takes its parts from feed belts on its south side and gives its products to collector belts on its north side, which run back west to the rack. The small squares are Splitters, the black diamonds Mergers. Click a machine for its position and settings, or a belt letter for what it carries.

Hall plan 5 · Tier 1

Parts hall on Hall 2

6 Constructor and 1 Assembler · 23.3 MW · north-west corner -1648, -440

Fed by one Siterite yard and one Callanite yard, it fills Storage Containers with the parts that buildings and milestones ask for most. The ingots it leaves over, and the yards' Concrete, go to containers of their own.

A bus hall. Every belt comes in or goes out through the south edge. A rack three belts high runs from that edge down the west wall; each row of machines takes its parts from feed belts on its south side and gives its products to collector belts on its north side, which run back west to the rack. The small squares are Splitters, the black diamonds Mergers. Click a machine for its position and settings, or a belt letter for what it carries.

Set it up, machine by machine

Lay the floor, stand the rack of Stackable Conveyor Poles along the west wall, then the machines in this order, which is the order the parts flow in. Tick each one as you build it; the page remembers. The numbers are the ones in the drawing.

Hall plan 8 · Tiers 3 and 4

Foundry on Lake Works, upper deck

6 Crusher, 6 Smelter, 4 Flexible Blast Furnace, 3 Sorter, 3 Reformer and 2 Constructor · 69.7 MW · north-west corner -1888, -496

The hot deck. Ore is crushed and sorted, melted in Flexible Blast Furnaces and cast in Reformers into Steel Rods, Steel Ingots and Brass Ingots; Smelters make the ingots the yards cannot cover. Molten metal, water, steam, air and flue gas travel in pipes; everything solid travels on belts.

A bus hall. Every belt comes in or goes out along the south side: ore along the gallery, cast metal down through the gallery floor to the Dock's rack, parts out through the south wall to the bank. A rack three belts high runs from that edge down the west wall; each row of machines takes its parts from feed belts on its south side and gives its products to collector belts on its north side, which run back west to the rack. The small squares are Splitters, the black diamonds Mergers. Click a machine for its position and settings, or a belt letter for what it carries.

Blueprints: the same builds on any ground

the same builds for any world, without a map

For a world that starts somewhere else: no map, just the machines, what goes in and what comes out. These are sized for a normal node (60 ore a minute); the site above doubles the Siterite yard because Iron A is pure. Click any block for the detail.

Build 1 · Opening yard, Siterite

Your first automatic lines. A Modular Miner has two outputs, and until Splitters arrive each output gets a line of its own: a Crusher, a Smelter, and a Constructor that turns the crushed stone into Concrete.

WhenAfter HUB Upgrade 5
Machines2 Crusher, 2 Constructor, 2 Smelter and 1 Modular Miner
Takes60 Siterite Ore a minute, one normal node
Makes30 Iron Ingot a minute, 8.33 Concrete a minute and 15 Tin Ingot a minute
Power15.3 MW
BeltsConveyor Belt Mk.1 everywhere; no Splitters or Mergers
FloorAbout 3 by 9 Foundations (24 by 72 m) with the machines in rows as drawn
  • Fit the Standard Mining Head to the miner first; it is a separate item in the build menu.
  • Each Crusher has one output for the crushed ore and one for the Crushed Gangue. Run the gangue to its Constructor and end each line in a Storage Container.
  • Both Crushers are set to 50%: each sees only one of the miner's two outputs.

Build 2 · Opening yard, Callanite

The same idea on the copper ore. One Smelter takes 24 crushed Callanite a minute, so each Crusher runs at 40% and the miner is not quite used up.

Machines2 Crusher, 2 Constructor, 2 Smelter and 1 Modular Miner
Takes48 Callanite Ore a minute, one normal node
Makes48 Copper Ingot a minute and 6.67 Concrete a minute
Power14.1 MW

FloorAbout 3 by 9 Foundations (24 by 72 m) with the machines in rows as drawn
  • Copper is needed in small amounts at this stage, so the 12 ore a minute the miner has left over does not matter.

Build 3 · Siterite yard

The Opening yard rebuilt once you have Splitters, Mergers and the Sorter. The Sorter separates crushed Siterite into iron, tin and stone, so the same 60 ore a minute gives half as much iron again, twice the tin and nearly twice the Concrete. Every output is used.

WhenAfter Tier 1, Ore Sorting

Takes60 Siterite Ore a minute, one normal node
Makes45 Iron Ingot a minute, 30 Tin Ingot a minute and 15 Concrete a minute
Power30.1 MW
BeltsConveyor Belt Mk.1 everywhere; 2 Splitters and 4 Mergers
FloorAbout 6 by 7 Foundations (48 by 56 m) with the machines in rows as drawn
  • Build it on the Opening yard's node: join the miner's two outputs with a Merger, set the Crusher to 100% and add the Sorter.
  • The Sorter has three outputs: Crushed Iron, Crushed Tin and Crushed Gangue. A Merger joins its gangue with the Crusher's on the way to the Constructor.

The copper yard at full strength: one Crusher feeding three Smelters through Splitters.

Fed by one Siterite yard and one Callanite yard, it fills Storage Containers with the parts that buildings and milestones ask for most. The ingots it leaves over, and the yards' Concrete, go to containers of their own.

Crosses

  • None: every sum came out.

Where the spare goes

Until 17 Nov 2026 two yards failed here. Hall 1 can make more Tin Ingot than the halls take, and the copper patch more Copper Ingot, and neither had anywhere to put it; a Sorter or a Crusher stops when one of its outlets cannot give, so the tin that backed up stopped the iron. The plan now has two stores on Hall 1's floor, in the ingot belts where they leave the Smelters:

  • Tin store, at -1744, -358.5: the tin that comes with the iron stays in it. A Storage Container in Tier 1; from Tier 2 an AWESOME Storage Mk.1, which sinks what does not fit.
  • Iron store, at -1757, -349.5: when it is full the yard slows to the iron the halls take. A Storage Container for good; nothing is lost.
  • The copper patch gets none: copper is the only thing a hall wants from it, so the yard just slows to what is taken.
  • A Conveyor Splitter to an AWESOME Sink would not do. A Splitter shares evenly, so a Sink that always takes has its full share before the halls have theirs. With the Parts hall resting, the Platform works wants 81% of the tin the yard then makes, and a Splitter would give it half.

Notes

  • Siterite yard: Tier 1 has nothing that destroys a part, so two ends can still fill. The Tin store, a Storage Container, is full 2 h 51 min from empty and 4 h 16 min each time it is emptied after that; then the yard slows to 19% and the Parts hall gets 16.9 Iron Ingots a minute of the 45 it wants. Bay 1 is full after 12 hours of Concrete that nobody uses; then both yards stop. From Tier 2 each of the two is an AWESOME Storage Mk.1, which sinks what reaches its last slot and never fills. That is the building's own description: nobody has watched one run.
  • Lakeside power station: the east Crusher is drawn using the outlet that Scott's own Crusher gives its second product by; its card says what to do if no powder leaves there.

On Foundations

  • Every works in the table stands on a floor of the plan. The miners stand on their nodes, as they must.
  • On the bare ground, still to be given a floor: 23 Storage Containers at the ends of belts (the Platform works' three, 3, the Kit row, 16, the Caterium bench's and the Lake Works', 4), and the Wind Turbines on the plateau.

What each tick stands for

  • Recipes: each machine's recipe is in the export, runs in that machine, and its rates were recomputed from the recipe, the count and the clock.
  • Unlocked: recipe and machine are handed out by the stage the works is built in.
  • Balance: what the machines make less what they use is what the works sends out and takes in, with nothing left over.
  • Belts: nothing carries more than the best belt of its stage: 60 on Mk.1, 120 on Mk.2, 270 on Mk.3.
  • Fed: a belt of the plan, or a node that gives that much, brings every input at every stage.
  • Taken away: every product has somewhere to go at every stage. A machine with two outlets stops when one cannot give, so in a yard the product the halls take most of sets the pace, and every other product ends in a store or a depot bay.
  • Power: recomputed from the machines, their clocks and the pack's own exponent.
  • Floor: the works stands on Foundations of the plan.

Built and standing (the server's world, 16 Nov 2026): the machines of the Siterite yard and the Callanite yard. Nobody has walked any other ground on this page. Not in any data, and so not checked: which outlet of a machine gives which product (one Crusher of Scott's has been read), what a Wind Turbine gives at its height, and the ground.

What is checked and what is not

what is verified and what is not
  • Checked by the page builder, every time it runs: each step of the path can be paid for with recipes unlocked before it; each machine in a build is unlocked by then; each build makes exactly what it says with nothing left over; no belt carries more than its tier allows; the builds before Logistics Mk. 2 need no Splitter or Merger; the yards cover what the halls take.
  • Where the numbers come from: the game data that the mod's authors publish on their wiki at k-mods.com, exported 2026-08-30 and read 2026-11-14: 580 recipes, 288 machine behaviours, 401 parts.
  • Checked for the site: every hall plan fits its floor; every floor is on the squares the survey shows clear (the copper patch has three contour squares, the terrace is the lake bank and says so); no floor covers a node, another floor or Main Street; the yards make at least what the halls take; the three belts drawn solid cross no rock edge and no deep water on the map.
  • Checked for the Lake Works: both decks stand on squares the survey shows as water (one has a shoal); both plans fit, the Foundry with its gallery; the Foundry casts exactly what the Dock takes, and with the yards covers every ingot; each node has the ore asked of it; no pipe carries more than a Pipeline Mk.1 allows; one extractor and one stack of each kind are enough; every leftover can be sunk; both causeways touch the deck and stand on no rock edge; every line in the kit table finishes inside the run; the four belts drawn solid in this stage cross no rock edge.
  • Built so far (the server's world, 16 Nov 2026): the Siterite yard on Hall 1, every machine within half a metre of its place, and the Callanite yard on the copper patch, within 0.7 m. No other hall stands yet.
  • Sizes and ports: every machine's size and where its inlets and outlets sit are read from the game itself, through the map's own mod. The two opening yards and the Callanite yard keep the places they were given before that, with each machine's true box drawn in the middle of its place; every other hall is laid out so that its belts meet the real inlets.
  • Not checked: the two dashed belts and the plateau's wind. The wiki's export may be older or newer than the version you have installed. The First jobs yard, the Twin Houses and the Lakeside power station stand on ground read from the map's picture; nobody has walked it.
  • Seen once: a Crusher gives each of its two products by an outlet of its own. Scott's Crusher by the Elevator pad has a belt on each outlet, and the box on the first holds 4,625 Crushed Larrussite and no stone. Which outlet gives which is not in the game's data: the plans follow that one Crusher, and their cards say what to do if a machine gives them the other way round.
  • Read, not seen: the AWESOME Storage Mk.1 that the Tin store and bay 1 become in Tier 2. Its size and its two belt ports are the game's own, the same as a Storage Container's; that it sinks what reaches its last slot is its description. If a full one ever backs its belt up, say so.
  • Assumed: that a Sorter does the same (its description says the output order is shown in the machine's menu), and that a normal node is the worst you will build on.
